thread:
Maya: Heads-up — the Python quickstart sample app surfaced a confusing exception: async client raises a bare RuntimeError instead of a structured HTTP/validation error.
Sam: I can reproduce. Server returns 400 but SDK just gives 'request failed' with no status or request_id. Blocks debugging for folks.
Maya: Minimal repro I used:
```py
from redwood import AsyncClient
import os
client = AsyncClient(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY'))
await client.responses.create(input=None)  # invalid on purpose
```
Sam: My log shows:
```
RuntimeError: request failed
  File ".../client.py", line 242, in _call
response body: {"error": "invalid_input", "request_id": "r-abc123"}
```
Julia: Looks like the async path drops the parsed error dict when re-raising. Sync client raises RequestError with .status and .raw_body.
Maya: This is onboarding friction—users can't map SDK exceptions to server request_id or status.
Sam: Fix proposal: add HTTPValidationError (subclass of HTTPError) for 4xx with attributes: status (int), raw_body (str), parsed (dict as JSON string), request_id (str). Ensure async re-raise preserves these.
Julia: Also ensure errors are typed in errors/__init__.py and include py.typed so "except redwood.errors.HTTPValidationError as e:" works with typing.
Maya: Test plan: add a tiny CI e2e in sampleapp that triggers a 400/422 and asserts e.request_id matches header. Covers regressions.
Sam: Filed issue https://github.com/redwood/repo/issues/4521 with repro and stack. Draft PR: github.com/redwood/repo/pull/789 (draft).
ci-bot: CI started for PR 789 — job: test-async-errors (queued) :hourglass_flowing_sand: 
Julia: I'll review and add type annotations. Can bump to P1 for DX.
Sam: I'll add changelog/migration note for users who depended on RuntimeError.
Maya: Thanks — will follow up when CI is green. :thumbsup:
